\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تعقیب} \fa{کردن} (ta'qib kardan)}{تعقیب کردن (ta'qib kardan)}]{\fa{تعقیب} \fa{کردن} (ta'qib kardan) — to chase, to pursue}

\label{lesson:FA-C317-taqib-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a pickpocket, then the Persian for a bag snatcher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تعقیب} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تعقیب} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ta'qib kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to chase, to pursue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{ماشین} \fa{دزد} \fa{را} \fa{تعقیب} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis mâshin-e dozd râ ta'qib kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police chased the thief's car.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{ta'qib mikonad}. In legal Persian also \textquotedblleft{}to prosecute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'qib} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ta'qīb} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}a following after\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'qib kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ta'qib kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a pickpocket, then the Persian for a bag snatcher, then say \emph{ta'qib kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قایم} \fa{شدن} (qâyem shodan)}{قایم شدن (qâyem shodan)}]{\fa{قایم} \fa{شدن} (qâyem shodan) — to hide (oneself)}

\label{lesson:FA-C317-qayem-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bag snatcher, then the Persian for to chase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قایم} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{قایم} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{qâyem shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to hide (oneself)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{پشت} \fa{درخت} \fa{قایم} \fa{شدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bachche-hâ posht-e derakht qâyem shodand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children hid behind the tree.
\end{quote}

Conversational. \emph{qâyem kardan} is \textquotedblleft{}to hide something\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{qâyem mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qâyem} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{qā'im}, \textquotedblleft{}standing, firm\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word); in Persian it came to mean \textquotedblleft{}tucked away\textquotedblright{}. \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qâyem shodan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a bag snatcher, then the Persian for to chase, then say \emph{qâyem shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گریختن} (gorikhtan)}{گریختن (gorikhtan)}]{\fa{گریختن} (gorikhtan) — to flee, to escape (literary)}

\label{lesson:FA-C317-gorikhtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to chase, then the Persian for to hide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گریختن}}
\textbf{\fa{گریختن}} (\emph{gorikhtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to flee, to escape (literary)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دزد} \fa{از} \fa{پنجره} \fa{گریخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dozd az panjere gorikht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief escaped through the window.
\end{quote}

Literary; in speech \emph{farâr kardan}. Present stem \emph{goriz-}: \emph{migorizad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gorikhtan} is a native Persian verb, with the present stem \emph{goriz-}. EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ناپدید} \fa{شدن} (nâpadid shodan)}{ناپدید شدن (nâpadid shodan)}]{\fa{ناپدید} \fa{شدن} (nâpadid shodan) — to disappear, to vanish}

\label{lesson:FA-C317-napadid-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to hide, then the Persian for to flee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ناپدید} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{ناپدید} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{nâpadid shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to disappear, to vanish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گربه} \fa{ما} \fa{دو} \fa{روز} \fa{ناپدید} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gorbe-ye mâ do ruz nâpadid shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our cat disappeared for two days.
\end{quote}

\emph{nâ-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} + \emph{padid} \textquotedblleft{}visible\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{nâpadid mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nâpadid} joins the native prefix \emph{nâ-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{padid} \textquotedblleft{}visible\textquotedblright{}; \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لو} \fa{رفتن} (low raftan)}{لو رفتن (low raftan)}]{\fa{لو} \fa{رفتن} (low raftan) — to be found out, to leak out}

\label{lesson:FA-C317-low-raftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to flee, then the Persian for to disappear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لو} \fa{رفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{لو} \fa{رفتن}} (\emph{low raftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be found out, to leak out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نقشه} \fa{آنها} \fa{زود} \fa{لو} \fa{رفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Naqshe-ye ânhâ zud low raft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Their plan was soon found out.
\end{quote}

Colloquial; the secret itself is the subject. Present \emph{low miravad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{raftan} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. The origin of \emph{low} \textquotedblleft{}revealed, exposed\textquotedblright{} is not settled; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
